purpose: Six-state census of every instrument this EP emits, across two domains. The `uninvoked`/`ambiguous` (Rust) and `harness_uninvoked`/`harness_unfalsified` (Python) arrays are MACHINE-GENERATED by audit_instruments.py --write-baseline and are drift-checked by --check. Everything under `hand` is hand-classified: `unreachable`, `misnamed`, `out-of-frame` and `absent` are not decidable from text.

domains.rust: rust/src, INSTRUMENT_FILES. Owner: Tank. Question: has this instrument got a production caller?
domains.harness: tests/, HARNESS_INSTRUMENT_FILES. Owner: Trinity. Question: has anything in the always-on lane ever watched this guard DISAGREE? Added at schema 2 because Guard D (assert_vulkan_executed_runtime) had four production callers from the day it landed -- the rust-domain question would have answered WIRED and been right -- and raised NameError at its first statement for its entire life, having never read a profiling event. Same census, same drift semantics, same vocabulary; one more state.

consumers: Trinity: M0 criterion 12 wiring census. Consume this file rather than building a second one.

states.uninvoked: exists, never called from production code (tests do not count)
states.unfalsified: HARNESS DOMAIN ONLY. Called, and possibly called often, but no always-on test has ever observed it in BOTH polarities -- rejecting a bad world AND accepting a good one. A guard that always passes, always crashes, or has inverted polarity is indistinguishable from a working one in this state. Later in the ordering than `uninvoked` because it survives the caller question; earlier than `unreachable` because a paired self-test settles it without hardware. Decided from the test AST: screened iff a non-GPU-gated test calls it inside pytest.raises(...) AND another non-gated test calls it outside one. Both are required -- a reject-only suite certifies a guard that rejects everything.
states.unreachable: called, but its output goes somewhere nothing reads
states.misnamed: wired, invoked, correct — and its name misdescribes its content
states.out-of-frame: wired, invoked, read, arithmetically correct - and the event it counts CANNOT OCCUR in the frame it observes, so its zero is not a measurement. Reports UNOBSERVABLE, never 0 (DESIGN.md 10.0.1 R12). A FIFTH state, not a split of `unreachable`: unreachable is fixed by wiring a reader, out-of-frame is fixed only by changing the world being measured (here, 6.5's one-VkDevice rule). Different repairs, so they must not share a name.

rulings.R13-is-not-a-seventh-state: RULED by Tank, 2026-08-01. R13 (an instrument's failure is spelled the same way as its finding) does NOT add a census state. Ask what a state is a property OF: all six above are properties of an instrument's POSITION IN THE SYSTEM -- does it exist, is it called, has it been seen to discriminate, does anything read it, can its event occur, does its name match. Guard D's own position was already covered: invoked and never in a position to report is `unreachable`, whose definition is exactly 'ran, produced nothing observable'. What R13 names is a property of the CHANNEL the verdict travels down -- pytest's summary line has a two-token alphabet and was carrying three states -- and that applies to every row of this census at once. An out-of-frame counter quoted through a two-token gate is misread exactly as badly as a crashed guard. A state that applies to all states is not a state; it is an axis. CONSEQUENCE, which is mechanical rather than taxonomic: audit_instruments.py now reports three terminal tokens (PASS=0, FAIL(drift)=1, ERROR(instrument)=2) and any escape from main() becomes ERROR(instrument), because before this a drift and a traceback left through the same door.
rulings.census-timeout-classification: RULED by Tank, 2026-08-01. `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` in tests/ops/test_wiring_census.py is ERROR(instrument), never FAIL(condition). The census is deterministic and byte-based: its answer does not depend on how loaded the box is, so a timeout is evidence about the box and none about the call graph. Under four-agent contention this box has been measured at 4.4x (708 s loaded vs 161 s quiet on the same suite), and a coordinator already misread the resulting timeouts as a 68-failure regression that did not exist. A lane that records a census timeout has NOT run the census, whatever else it reports, and must not be counted as a detection in either direction. Trinity owns the timeout value; this classification is Tank's and is not negotiable by raising the timeout.

harness_notes.state: SCREENED - the only one, as of 2026-07-31
harness_notes.artifact: tests/ops/test_guard_d.py: 12 always-on tests, no GPU, no model, synthesised ORT profiling JSON. Negative polarity (zero VulkanEP Node events -> AssertionError), positive polarity (one event -> returns 1), plus four MUTANT guards that must each FAIL the same protocol - including a byte-accurate reconstruction of the NameError defect that shipped.
harness_notes.why_it_needed_this: It had four production callers from the day it landed and had never read a profiling event. The rust-domain question ('has it got a caller?') answers WIRED and is correct. On merge the suite went 8 passed -> 5 failed and that redness was reported to the team as 'Guard D works'; it was crashing. A guard that raises NameError and a guard that correctly detects a fallback are indistinguishable to every reader we have.

harness_notes.excludes: nothing arithmetically - it counts exactly what it says. The hazard is the READING: ORT emits one Node event per FUSED ISLAND, and on Phi-3.5 354 of 364 graph nodes execute inside ONE island. out_of_frame.artifact: the counters JSON, and the authoritative-audit sentence in every staging_verdict() branch
out_of_frame.excludes: everything, in the SPLIT-DEVICE and OFF frames. The counter can only move when the engine binds one of the provider's buffers, and while the provider holds its own VkDevice (6.5) no dispatch on the session's device can bind them at all. The zero was being read as 'residency has not landed yet'; it actually meant 'this question has no answer in this run'.
out_of_frame.disposition: FIXED. The artifact emits the JSON string "UNOBSERVABLE" instead of the number 0 whenever alloc_device_frame != SHARED, so a reader doing arithmetic on it fails loudly. New keys alloc_device_frame / alloc_device_frame_device carry frame provenance; epctl prints the frame on the --require-device-memory PASS path. Falsifiers: counters::a_pinned_authoritative_counter_reports_unobservable_and_never_zero, allocator::a_zero_authoritative_count_in_a_foreign_frame_says_unobservable_not_unwired, allocator::a_nonzero_authoritative_count_in_a_split_frame_is_not_credible.

out_of_frame.excludes: vk::session's staging copies, ALL of them. It counts only copies made by the allocator's own provider, on the provider's own VkDevice, and only with ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_DEVICE_MEMORY=1. It read 0 on a run whose cmd_upload phase was 15.2 s. Both numbers correct; different worlds - R12's specimen.
out_of_frame.disposition: NOT renamed: it is correct in its own frame, and compatibility outranks elegance. Tagged instead, by alloc_device_frame. The session-side accounting is the separate, unconditional session_staging_upload_bytes. The two must NEVER be added.

ledger.quarantine: UNOBSERVED, not clean: peak depth 423 against a window of 4096, retired 0, use_after_free 0. The detector was NOT exhausted (peak is 10% of the window), so use_after_free == 0 is a genuine negative for this pattern — 'we checked', not 'we could not have seen it'. Distinct from quarantine_retired, which was 'we could not have seen it' until it was plumbed off the GetStats path.
ledger.alloc_device_authoritative_spans: UNOBSERVABLE, not 0, as of 6.5's ruling: structurally pinned while the memory provider holds a second VkDevice, and R12 forbids any criterion naming a pinned instrument - so M1's weight-residency criterion is read against device_upload_bytes on the session's device instead. It passes through THREE distinct states and each gets its own sentence: UNOBSERVABLE (no frame in which a result could exist) -> UNWIRED zero (frame SHARED, but allocator::tally::on_device_authoritative still has no production caller) -> a measurement (transfer::device_buffer_for called). The word 'zero' never appears alone.

states_ordering: absent -> uninvoked -> unfalsified (harness) -> unreachable -> out-of-frame -> misnamed, by how late the failure is discoverable. R10's screen catches the first two mechanically. `unfalsified` is the third mechanical one and is the harness domain's whole contribution: it is decidable from the test AST, it needs no hardware, and it is the only state that would have caught Guard D -- which passed the caller question cleanly while crashing on its first statement. Nothing but a second, independent instrument catches the last two.
